findings.title: String#ends_with? does not exist — NoMethodError when website host is parent of instance host
findings.body: Ruby's String class defines `end_with?`, not `ends_with?`. In the else branch of `website_name` (e.g. website host `example.com` vs instance host `forums.example.com` — exactly the scenario covered by the new spec 'website domain is parent of instance domain'), calling `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` raises NoMethodError, so serializing such a user raises a 500. The new spec for that case would fail with this code; it must be `end_with?`.

findings.title: include_website_name missing '?' suffix, so the inclusion guard never runs
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only consults predicates named `include_<attr>?`. The method is defined as `def include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is ignored and `website_name` is always serialized (as null when the website is blank). Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: website_name leaks the website of TL0 users to anonymous viewers
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, which hides a TL0 user's profile fields from anonymous visitors (scope.restrict_user_fields?). The new `website_name` attribute is not added to that list and its include guard only checks `website.present?`, so anonymous viewers now receive the TL0 user's website host (and path) via `website_name` even though `website` itself is hidden — defeating the purpose of the restriction. `website_name` should be included in `untrusted_attributes`.

findings.title: Host comparison is case-sensitive and ignores default ports
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s).host` preserves the case of the entered URL (e.g. `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` yields `EXAMPLE.com`), which will not equal `Discourse.current_hostname` and will fall through to the 'different domain' branch, hiding the path. Downcase both hosts before comparing. Additionally `URI(...).host` raises URI::InvalidURIError for URLs without a scheme (e.g. `example.com/user` parses with nil host, so it silently returns nil — acceptable but means scheme-less websites never show a path), which may be worth handling explicitly rather than via a blanket rescue.
